reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch resolve Ecclesiastes' praise of mourning over mirth by limiting Qohelet's commended enjoyment to pleasure conditioned on the fear of God.

sides.snippet: Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good.
sides.verseText: Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good.

sides.snippet: Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be joyful:
sides.verseText: Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be joyful: for that will accompany him in his labor all the days of his life which God has given him under the sun.
